thread:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: High error rate for customer Xenon (vpc-xn-01, dedicated pool) — 5xx spike, tps falling back. Alerts: latency > 2s, error_rate > 10% — triggered 2523456789

mira: ack — I'm taking lead. oncall: @eng-oncall are you able to join for memory/connection symptoms?

eng-oncall: joining. quick check: running `kubectl get pods -n xenon-pool` shows 3/5 pods `CrashLoopBackOff` on model-serving containers. attaching recent logs.

sam: copying logs paste —
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:02Z] model-server: OOMKilled while allocating KV cache (8GB)
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] healthcheck: failing 503 -> restarting
[2026-03-15T09:12:15Z] autoscaler: scaleup requested but quota denied for pool xenon-dedicated
```

alex: looks like a memory leak / KV cache growth under long-context requests. Xenon has pinned quantized latest-7b on pool.

mira: immediate mitigation options: 1) Evict heavy tenants from xenon pool to fallback shared pool; 2) Force-restart model processes with reduced KV size; 3) Add temporary burst nodes from shared capacity. Which is fastest?

jordan: I can push routing override to send new sessions to shared-fallback in ~3 min. Will that avoid data residency concerns for Xenon?

kate-cs: customer Xenon requires VPC-only by contract for production. Any routing to shared-fallback (hosted) requires legal review — need explicit exec approval.

mira: ok, do not route off-VPC. Option 2 then: restart with reduced KV and limit max_seq to 1024. eng-oncall, can you craft the restart command?

eng-oncall: patching deployment with env override: `KV_MAX_STORE=1G MAX_SEQ_LEN=1024` then rolling restart. Applying now.

ops-bot: deploy-bot triggered rollout xenon-dedicated@rev-20260315-6f2a applied by eng-oncall

sam: monitoring pod restarts — pods are re-attaching, error rate trending down from 12% -> 2% in 6m. latency from p95 2.4s -> 1.1s.

kate-cs: Customer outreach — I drafted a short ack to send now (holding until we confirm stabilization):

kate-cs: "Hi Xenon team — we detected degraded performance on your dedicated pool this morning. Our engineers are applying a mitigation that will temporarily limit session lengths to stabilize service while we investigate. We'll follow up with an RCA and timeline for permanent fix. — Kate, CSM"

mira: good. Send after we hit 30m stable. Also prep exec note and potential SLA credit calc.

alex: root cause hypothesis: KV cache growth + autoscaler quota limits prevented safe scale up, causing OOMs. Long-context endpoints from a single tenant triggered repeated cache fills. We'll need to patch runtime to cap KV growth and add per-tenant memory accounting.

mira: creating follow-up action items:
- ACTION-1: eng: implement per-tenant KV cap + telemetry (owner: alex)
- ACTION-2: infra: increase emergency quota or enable cross-pool burst for dedicated customers (owner: sam)
- ACTION-3: cs/legal: draft customer comms + check contract for off-VPC mitigations (owner: kate-cs & legal-bot)
- ACTION-4: ops: prepare exec brief and SLA credit estimate (owner: jordan)

ops-bot: incident severity set to Sev2 by mira — impact: Xenon production degraded, partial request failures, customers on dedicated pool only.

sam: quick calc for SLA: Xenon has 99.9% monthly uptime guarantee. They experienced ~45 minutes of degraded availability across a 24-hour window (based on our telemetry). Preliminary credit = (minutes_downtime / total_month_minutes) * monthly_fee * SLA_multiplier. I'll attach a precise sheet.

mira: for exec note, keep it short: 1) what happened, 2) mitigation, 3) customer impact, 4) next steps + ETA. Jordan, can you draft?

jordan: draft below — feedback welcome:

"Executive summary: On 2026-03-15 09:12 UTC, Xenon's dedicated inferencing pool experienced memory exhaustion leading to pod restarts and ~45m of elevated error rates. Mitigation: we applied a runtime cap reducing KV cache and restarted affected pods; service stabilized within 10 minutes and returned to normal by 09:58 UTC. Impact: Partial 5xx responses for subset of sessions in production (no data exfiltration). Next steps: patch runtime to enforce per-tenant caps, enable emergency burst capacity for dedicated pools, and provide formal RCA and SLA credit calc within 3 business days"

mira: looks good. Add note that routing off-VPC was considered but disallowed by contract — included for transparency.

kate-cs: legal-bot — please confirm if contract forbids routing to shared-hosted fallback; if there is any leeway for emergency failover.

legal-bot: Reviewing clause 4.2 (data residency & VPC isolation). No automatic routing off-VPC is permitted without written customer consent. Emergency exception requires VP-approval and CTO signoff.

mira: noted. we'll avoid off-VPC. Kate, please send the customer ack once we hit 30m stable (we're at ~18m now). Jordan, prep exec email to leadership after CS sends customer ack.

sam: logging follow-ups — I opened GH issue: redwood/runtime#7892 "per-tenant kv cap + telemetry" and assigned to alex.

alex: thanks, started prototype patch. rough plan: cap cache by tracking per-tenant bytes and evict LRU entries beyond threshold; unit tests + perf eval, estimate 5 working days for rollout to prod.

kate-cs: sending ack now. (copied)

kate-cs: "Sent to Xenon at 09:45 UTC — they'll acknowledge and requested a dedicated postmortem meeting tomorrow 16:00 UTC."

mira: excellent. closing incident channel for live mitigation. We'll reconvene for RCA draft. Next touch: internal RCA draft in #eng-runtime by EOD tomorrow.

ops-bot: incident annotated: severity Sev2 -> mitigated, mitigation_time=2523456945, mitigated_by=mira

jordan: prepping SLA credit estimate doc, will post link when ready.

sam: posting monitoring dashboard snapshot: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/xenon/pool/2523456789

mira: thanks everyone. follow-up owners keep updates in the RCA thread.
